**Finding: Missing insurance provision (INSURANCE, low severity)**

The Agreement has no insurance clause at all — a search for "insurance" returns nothing, and the general provisions (Sections 15–30) end with Force Majeure without any coverage requirement. This matters because TrueLink hosts our Web Site and processes Client Content and Credit Data (raw consumer credit information from the repositories), which is exactly the profile the playbook treats as requiring E&O and cyber/privacy cover; the walk-away position is no insurance for a vendor processing personal data.

**Redline (validated, ok:true):** new Section 31 inserted after Section 30 (p0097) requiring TrueLink, at its own expense, throughout the term and for one year thereafter, to carry CGL of USD 1M per occurrence / 2M aggregate, E&O of USD 2M, cyber/privacy of USD 5M covering its handling of Client Content and Credit Data, and statutory workers' compensation, with certificates of insurance on request.

**Comment:** [Playbook] The Agreement has no insurance provision even though TrueLink hosts our Web Site and handles Client Content and Credit Data, so we have added our standard coverages (CGL USD 1M/2M, E&O USD 2M, cyber USD 5M, statutory workers' compensation) with certificates on request. If USD 5M cyber is not available, we can accept E&O of USD 1M and cyber of USD 2M.

One point to flag for the negotiation: Section 24's survival list covers "Sections 1 and 5 through 30," so the new Section 31 falls outside it — the one-year tail is built into the clause text itself, but you may want to conform the survival list if the counterparty opens Section 24 for other reasons.
